title: Noah and the promise
summary: Relive Noah's story in 3D, then keep your promise to Grandma Ruth before the storm… even when others laugh at you.

trait.name: Faithfulness
trait.description: Being faithful means keeping your word and trusting God, even when it's hard or when others make fun of you.
trait.jesus: Jesus trusted his Father all the way, out of love for us. And he keeps his promises: "I am with you always."

objectives.intro: Go and see the Keeper: he has a story to show you.
objectives.animals: Bring the animals, two by two, to the ark's ramp.
objectives.board: Climb into the ark too, up the ramp.
objectives.promise: Grandma Ruth needs you: go and see her near her pen.
objectives.goats: Bring the three sheep back into the pen before the storm.
objectives.thanks: Grandma Ruth is back: go and talk to her.

intro.text: Today I won't just tell you a story. I'll let you live it!
Close your eyes… Imagine… We are very, very long ago.

story.text: A very long time ago, people on earth were doing a lot of harm. They had forgotten God.
But one man, Noah, loved God and listened to him. God said to him: "Build a great ark, a huge wooden boat."
"A flood is coming. I want to protect you, your family and the animals."
Noah obeyed. He built the ark for years, when there wasn't a single cloud in the sky! Go and talk to Noah.

askHelp.text: Hello! You've come just in time, I need help.
People laughed at me: "A boat, here, so far from the sea?" But God asked me to, and I trust him.
God told me to bring the animals in two by two. Go near the stag and the doe, the horses and the zebras: they will follow you to the ark's ramp.

allIn.text: Well done! All the animals are safe.
I'm going into the ark. Come quickly, the first drops are falling!

flood.text: God himself closes the door of the ark. Then the rain begins to fall…
It rains for forty days and forty nights. Water covers the whole earth.
But inside the ark, Noah, his family and the animals are safe. God has not forgotten them.
One day, the rain stops. Noah sends out a dove. It comes back with an olive leaf in its beak: dry land has returned!
Everyone comes out of the ark. And a rainbow appears in the sky.
God says: "This is the sign of my promise: never again will a flood destroy the earth." God always keeps his promises.

promise.text: Ah, there you are! I have to go and visit my sister, on the other side of the hill.
The sky is turning grey… My three sheep are wandering around the city. Can you promise to bring them back into the pen before the storm?
Thank you. I know I can count on you.

tease.text: Hey! Forget those sheep and come and play with us!
It's never going to rain, look at the sky! You're tiring yourself out for nothing!
I promised Grandma Ruth. A promise is a promise… even when others laugh.

storm.text: The last sheep is barely inside when the rain starts pouring down!
The sheep are nice and dry. The children run for shelter.
You were right… You kept your promise. Well done!
Then the sun comes back, and a rainbow stretches over Zion, like a promise.

thanks.text: My sheep are all here, safe and sound! You kept your word.
When someone keeps their promises, you can trust them. You're like Jesus, you know.

debrief.text: Noah trusted God before he saw a single drop of rain. And you kept your promise even when others laughed.
God is faithful: he never forgets what he has promised. Jesus told us: "I am with you always."
A faithful watcher is someone others can count on. Thank you for being one!

noe.text: Keep going! The stag and the doe, two horses, two zebras. They're waiting for your help!

moqueur1.text: We're playing tag! Want to join?

moqueur2.text: Look at that lovely sky… well, almost blue.

ending.message: God always keeps his promises. Being faithful like Jesus means keeping your word and trusting God, even when it's hard.
ending.reflection: Noah obeyed before he saw any rain, probably while being mocked. Have you ever kept a promise when it was hard? Which promise of God gives you confidence today?

life.bibleWhere: Genesis is the very first book of the Bible, at the start of the Old Testament. Noah's story begins in chapter 6. You can read chapter 9, verses 8 to 17: the rainbow promise.
life.bibleQuestion: In chapter 9, God makes a promise with the rainbow. What is the promise? Who does God make it to?
life.prayer: Lord, thank you for always keeping your promises. Help me to trust you, even when it's hard, and to keep my word like you. Amen.
life.challenge: This week, make a simple promise and keep it to the end: tidy your room, help at home, call a grandparent.
life.followup: So, did you keep your promise this week?
life.verse: Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.
family: For little ones: what did God put in the sky to show he keeps his promise?
For older ones: Noah built the ark before he saw the rain. What does it mean to trust?
For everyone: which promise of God reassures our family?
life.activity: Draw a big rainbow. On each colour, write a promise of God or a promise you want to keep as a family.
